title: Caption Wrap
statement: A video player shows captions in lines at most `width` characters wide. The words in `text` are separated by single spaces.

Fill lines greedily: add the next word to the current line, with one space before it, as long as the line stays within `width`; otherwise start a new line. A word longer than `width` is first cut into pieces of exactly `width` characters, with the last piece holding whatever is left, and each piece is then treated as its own word.

examples.input: text = "the quick brown fox jumps", width = 10

examples.explanation: The long word is cut into "supercal", "ifragili", and "stic", and "yo" still fits after the last piece.

constraints: text is lowercase words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing spaces

hints: Deal with the too-long words first. If you cut them into width-sized pieces up front, every remaining word fits on a line by itself.
Then keep the current line and its length. A word fits if the line is empty, or if length + 1 + the word's length is at most width.
Don't forget to add the last line at the end, and don't add an empty line when the text is empty.
pitfalls: Forgetting the space when checking whether the next word fits.
Adding an empty line at the start or end.
Cutting long words into pieces that are off by one character.
interviewerNotes: See whether they ask how words longer than width are handled before coding. It's the main ambiguity.
Have them test a line that fits exactly, like "one two" with width 7.
Follow-up: how would you lay out lines to minimize ragged right edges instead of filling greedily? Discussion only, it's a dynamic programming problem.
